        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC marker-based shape replication (task-c657d49c observations)",
        "content": "Observed three demos from task-c657d49c. Sparse marker pixels (color 8 or 5) in uniform-background ARC grids are replaced by translated copies of a separate colored shape; demos suggest preserve template color(s), and infer copy alignment from the marker’s relative position to the source shape. Demo 1: source multicolor pattern 7/9 copied at every 8-marker location. Demo 2: a 3-color block-and-tail source was copied at every 5-marker; each marker aligned at offset (+2 rows,+1 col) from copy top-left. Demo 3: 3x3 blocks of color 3 copied at 6-marker positions, with marker aligned top-row center. Thus alignment varies with shape/task, and must be inferred from demonstrations/source geometry rather than assuming marker is top-center or top-left. This instance was not solved; avoid the unsupported assumption that a multicolor shape including outlier colors is replicated intact, and use demo placement evidence carefully. Validate output dimensions and every row length before submitting.",

        "title": "ARC marker-stencil replication in noisy grids",
        "content": "In ARC grids with a noisy two-color field and a small connected object in a third color, consider whether the object is a stencil to replicate. Record the marker object's occupied-cell offsets and color. At each in-bounds translation where every stencil-occupied position in the original grid is background zero, recolor those positions with the marker color. Preserve all other cells, including the original marker and noisy nonzero cells; overlapping matches form a union. Evidence: three demos and a successful test solve for task-3ca7e4c6. In its test, the marker color was 9 and the offsets were {(0,0),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1)}; the replicated color was 9, not the dominant noisy-grid color 2.",

        "title": "ARC full-line divider repositions shape with 8 marker",
        "content": "Observed task-5b815ceb. Transform by moving the shape along the axis perpendicular to the divider to the side nearest the divider, placed immediately adjacent to the divider. Draw a full-length color-8 line in the shape’s former adjacent position on the far side of the relocated shape (equivalently: the 8 line marks the boundary beyond the shape, opposite the divider). Preserve divider and all other background. Demo vertical case: divider col3, shape rows5-13 cols9-11 moves to cols4-6 (immediately right of divider), line 8 col7; original shape area cleared. Test horizontal case: divider row9, shape 9s row5 cols0-1 moves to row8; full row7 becomes 8.         "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC noisy grid: remove isolated intrusions and repair rectangular objects",
        "content": "In ARC grids with a dominant uniform background and solid rectangular objects of various colors, isolated contaminant cells outside objects should be restored to the background, and contaminant pixels or holes inside true rectangles should be replaced with the rectangle's color. First catalogue each candidate rectangle's exact bounding box from its repeated solid row and column runs; do not extend across blank separators or infer bounds from nearby objects. In task-18ac0783, the validated rectangles were: color 5 at rows 4–10, columns 2–3; color 5 at rows 4–10, columns 9–12; color 9 at rows 0–2, columns 11–13; color 9 at rows 4–10, columns 6–7; color 9 at rows 12–17, columns 5–11; color 9 at rows 16–21, columns 13–15; color 9 at rows 17–20, columns 0–1; and color 5 at rows 22–23, columns 7–10. The first color-5 object is only two columns wide, not four; overextending its bounds caused repeated wrong submissions. Demos confirm the general operation: preserve and repair solid rectangles, clear isolated off-object noise.",

        "content": "Observed task-8c5dcdc7 with 8 demo pairs. Background uniform; several disconnected non-background objects and isolated pixels of several colors. Transform changes only a selected portion: e.g. demo 1 changed one color-7 component to color 9; demo2 changed a small color-7 component to 0; demo3 changed a single color-7 pixel to 8; demo4 changed a color-3 object to 0; demo5 changed a color-0 L-triomino to 8; demo6 changed one isolated color-6 pixel to 4; demo7 changed a short vertical color-7 component to 6; demo8 changed one isolated color-7 pixel to 3. The operation is selective recoloring, but the selection/recolor rule was not identified reliably. Do not assume all pixels of a color/component should be recolored. Compare demos for matching shapes, adjacency, and spatial correspondence; inspect which exact component/pixel changes.       "arc_offset_divider_panels_extend_marker_rays_and_project_lines": {
        "id": "arc_offset_divider_panels_extend_marker_rays_and_project_lines",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC offset divider panels extend marker rays and project lines",
        "content": "Observed task-d3b18386 with six demos. Rule: a large uniform-background grid has two same-color straight divider/border segments on opposite sides, parallel and offset along their length. A distinct marker color (various demos: 0, 5, 7, 8, 9) appears on one side. The pattern is projected into the opposite panel by the offset between divider segments, and source markers become color 4. For each source marker row/column, extend the marker color from the nearby border side up to (but not including) the marker; replace marker with 4. In the corresponding translated row/column in the opposite panel, fill the full span from one edge to the opposite divider with marker color. Preserve divider lines, other cells, and background. Orientation generalizes: horizontal divider segments cause vertical displacement/projection; vertical segments cause horizontal runs/projection. Validate exact offset and edge extents from divider segment endpoints. Confirmed test: left color-2 vertical segment rows1..8 at col0, right segment rows9..16 at col19 (offset +8); color-5 markers at (r,c)=(1,16),(3,7),(4,6),(5,5),(7,4),(8,16). Each source row had 5 filled from c1 to c-1, marker changed to 4; translated rows 9,11,12,13,15,16 were filled color 5 across c0..18, with right border col19 preserved. Important lesson from failed hypotheses: do NOT fill source marker rows past marker toward the far edge; source ray runs from adjacent divider toward the marker. Translated rows include the background-side edge cell (e.g. col0) but stop before the opposite colored divider. Demo5 verifies vertical arrangement with markers in lower panel projecting upward; demo4 verifies same rule rotated.",
